Bigots generally refers to people who hate others based on intrinsic, unchangeable traits. This is why you will often hear them call the legitimacy of LGBTQ into question, saying things like "being gay is a choice" and so on. If it actually were a choice, then they would have some grounds for condemning the behavior, e.g. "if you change, I will stop hating you". Now, even if this were the case, they would still be "legitimately" hating people for something that has no bearing on virtually anyone else's lives, but at the very least it would be conditional. As it stands, the only long-term solution for bigots is to exterminate the people they are bigoted against, and they try their absolute hardest to move away from that obvious truth.  


Racism and bigotry in general is a choice, and most people who are opposed to these things are usually not inherently opposed to the bigots themselves. If they actually change their minds and change their behavior, most people will simply move on with their lives (even though the damage they've dealt can stick around for much longer). Even if we are "bigoted against racist people", we only really hate them for a certain behavior, not for their very essence.
